TAX ON NATURAL GAS EXPORTS-GOVERNMENT POSITION
speechtext: Madam Speaker, my question is to the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance. Is the government considering imposing or discussing with producing provinces a tax on the export of Canadian natural gas which would bring to the federal government treasury all or part of the difference between the domestic gas price and those prices now received from the United States for Canadian gas exported to that country?

speakerposition: Deputy Prime Minister; Minister of Finance
subtopic: TAX ON NATURAL GAS EXPORTS-GOVERNMENT POSITION
speechtext: Madam Speaker, as far as I, myself, am concerned, I have had no discussions with respect to a tax such as the hon. member suggests, and certainly no decision has been taken along those lines. If one were to be taken, obviously it would be a tax change that would be announced in the usual way. But by saying that I am not even suggesting that the hon. member ought to expect it.

speechtext: What is the usual way?

subsubtopic: ACCESS OF MANUFACTURED GOODS TO JAPANESE MARKETS
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, my question is also for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance. It concerns our economic relations with Japan.
In light of the fact that there is such a substantial imbalance in our trade relations with Japan, not in a monetary sense but in the sense that we export, by and large, raw products to Japan and import about $2 billion worth of finished products, is the minister in a position to tell us what specific proposals have been put to the Japanese delegation led by their prime minister, who is now in Canada, to correct this imbalance and ensure that Canada's manufactured goods have access to Japanese markets?

speakerposition: Deputy Prime Minister; Minister of Finance
subsubtopic: ACCESS OF MANUFACTURED GOODS TO JAPANESE MARKETS
speechtext: Madam Speaker, the Government of Canada, certainly through negotiations which we had in connection with GATT, pressed very hard, as did other countries, to secure additional access to the Japanese market for additional processed Canadian goods. As my hon. friend knows, there was very strong resistance at that time. None of the industrialized countries, including the European Community, achieve the access to the Japanese market that was required. These points, obvioulsy, were repeated in the discussions yesterday with the Japanese prime minister.

speechtext:

We know that Canadian manufacturers are being hurt by the Buy America policy in the United States, and we know that there are discussions under way at the moment concerning those laws. I should like to get an assurance from the Deputy Prime Minister as to the representations being made by the Canadian government with respect to Japanese non-tariff barriers, since we are leaving ourselves open to tremendous penetration by Japanese exporters if we are not able to have access to Japanese markets for our manufactured goods.

subsubtopic: STATUS OF STUDY ON KOOTENAY LAKE WATER QUALITY
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, my question is addressed to the Minister of State for Science and Technology and Minister of the Environment. It is in relation to the Kootenay Lake water quality study, long being conducted by the inland waters directorate of his department.
In view of the importance of this long-delayed report to both the fishery and tourist industry in and around Kootenay Lake, which is already facing closure, and having regard to the effects which the report's findings may have on international negotiations regarding possible Columbia River treaty mitigations, current Kootenay River flows at Libby Dam, and B.C. Hydro's plans for the Kootenay River diversion, would the minister kindly inform the House as to the current status of
May 6, 1980

this report and when we can expect the official report to finally see the light of day?

speakeroldname: Hon. John Roberts (Minister of State for Science and Technology and Minister of the Environment):
speakerposition: Minister of the Environment; Minister of State for Science and Technology
subsubtopic: STATUS OF STUDY ON KOOTENAY LAKE WATER QUALITY
speechtext: Madam Speaker, I am informed that the report should be available publicly by the end of this month.

subsubtopic: STATUS OF STUDY ON KOOTENAY LAKE WATER QUALITY
speechtext: Madam Speaker, it is certainly reassuring, after more than a year, to hear that. In view of the fact that the release of this important report was originally scheduled for the spring of 1979-later, assurances were given by officers of the department, in committee, that it would be available for publication on July 1 of last year-and having regard to widespread suspicions that the report is being altered or tampered with to suit the designs of either B.C. Hydro or the B.C. government, will the minister undertake to launch an immediate investigation in order to ascertain the real reasons for this unconscionable delay and to determine whether the report has, in fact, been altered to suit the needs of B.C. Hydro's latest plan of attack on the interests of the people of Kootenay West and Kootenay East-Revelstoke?

speakerposition: Minister of the Environment; Minister of State for Science and Technology
subsubtopic: STATUS OF STUDY ON KOOTENAY LAKE WATER QUALITY
speechtext: To the best of my knowledge, Madam Speaker, the assertions of the hon. member are false. As I said to him in my first answer, my expectation is that the report will be published by the end of this month. He can then make whatever judgments he himself would like to make.

subsubtopic: INQUIRY WHETHER CULTURAL AFFAIRS COMMITTEE STILL ACTIVE
speechtext:
Madam
Speaker, my question is directed to the Secretary of State. As his predecessor in that portfolio, the Hon. David MacDonald, had set up a committee made up of representatives of various fields of cultural activity, committee whose purpose was to re-evaluate the Canadian policy in that particular sector, and because of the favourable reaction to the creation of that committee of the various groups interested, can the minister tell the House whether that committee is still active, when it will present its reports, and whether he intends to refer the report of the committee to the House Standing Committee on Communications and Culture?

speakeroldname: Hon. Francis Fox (Secretary of State and Minister of Communications):
speakerposition: Secretary of State of Canada; Minister of Communications
subsubtopic: INQUIRY WHETHER CULTURAL AFFAIRS COMMITTEE STILL ACTIVE
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, 1 thank the hon. member for his question and take the opportunity to advise him that the committee in question is still at work and holding hearings; it continued holding hearings during the last few months. I had the opportunity of meeting the committee and taking part twice in its sittings this last month. However, the committee is not in a position to present its report to the Secretary of State
Oral Questions
and will not be for a few months yet. At this point, I intend to encourage the committee, once its preliminary report is completed, to hold public hearings throughout the country, in order to complete its preliminary report precisely in light of the recommendations that may be made to it by the various interested groups from all over Canada, and have the report referred later on, as completed, to the parliamentary committee.

subsubtopic: HARMFUL DRUG AND ANTIBIOTIC RESIDUES IN MEAT
speechtext: Madam Speaker, I direct my question to the Minister of Agriculture. In view of the fact that harmful drug and antibiotic residues are still being found in meat and meat products passed for human consumption, with serious consequences for those consumers who are allergic to specific drugs and antibiotics, what action has been taken by the food production and inspection branch of Agriculture Canada to ensure the absence of such harmful drug residues from meat and meat products emanating from abattoirs under federal inspection?

speakeroldname: Hon. E. F. Whelan (Minister of Agriculture):
subsubtopic: HARMFUL DRUG AND ANTIBIOTIC RESIDUES IN MEAT
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, I have checked into the matter of the inspections and I feel that I must disagree somewhat with the hon. member's statement about harmful side effects. Recent figures which I have viewed show that several thousand such tests have taken place, none of which has concluded that there are harmful residues present in the different meat products which have been inspected.
My department is continuing its vigilance of the product. I feel confident that everything possible is being done. We are not letting up on the program but are actually stepping it up.

subsubtopic: HARMFUL DRUG AND ANTIBIOTIC RESIDUES IN MEAT
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, 1 would like to thank the minister for his answer. However, according to a recent report which I have received, approximately 14 per cent of all inspected meat and poultry sold for human consumption in Canada contains drug residues. Certainly this is indicative that the present testing for residues is either insufficient, inaccurate, or both.
Will the minister take the necessary action to make available to the food production and inspection branch of Agriculture Canada whatever else may be needed in manpower, equipment, etc., to step up and increase this important service in all federally inspected abattoirs?

subsubtopic: HARMFUL DRUG AND ANTIBIOTIC RESIDUES IN MEAT
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, I have before me, in my briefing books, thousands of these tests. 1 will make them available to the hon. member if he does not already have the information. If he, after viewing these reports, still feels that there are some things which are not being done properly, and

May 6, 1980
Oral Questions
if he can prove his statements, I will be glad to review the matter.

subsubtopic: INCENTIVES TO ENCOURAGE EXPLORATION FOR ENERGY
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, my question is to the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance. The chairman of Dome Petroleum has been quoted recently as saying that Dome has been given assurances that some kind of incentive will be granted to encourage frontier exploration.
Instead of giving such assurances to Dome Petroleum-a company which had a 50 per cent increase in profits in the first quarter of this year-will the minister assure the people of Canada that any new measures which he introduces will not allow such companies to make windfall profits at the taxpayers' expense?

speakeroldname: Hon. Allan J. MacEachen (Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance):
speakerposition: Deputy Prime Minister; Minister of Finance
subsubtopic: INCENTIVES TO ENCOURAGE EXPLORATION FOR ENERGY
speechtext: Madam Speaker, the hon. member is obviously referring to the cancellation of the super-depletion allowance. He also knows that an announcement was made by the Minister of Energy, Mines and Resources and myself to the effect that that particular allowance would be replaced, or that consideration would be given to replacing it with an expenditure program. When this program is in place, it will not be necessary for the hon. member to worry about windfall profits through that particular source.

subsubtopic: INCENTIVES TO ENCOURAGE EXPLORATION FOR ENERGY
speechtext: Madam Speaker, super-depletion is another name for incentive for these oil companies. The chairman of Dome Petroleum has also been quoted as saying the company is confident that their profit picture will follow the upward trend set in the first quarter of this year. Will the minister table documents in the House which will prove that the oil companies do, in fact, need such extensive incentives and tax breaks?

speakerposition: Deputy Prime Minister; Minister of Finance
subsubtopic: INCENTIVES TO ENCOURAGE EXPLORATION FOR ENERGY
speechtext: Madam Speaker, the proposal to which I have referred deals with the replacement of the super-depletion allowance which was intended to encourage frontier exploration through a new expenditure program. It seems to me that that would take care of the concern which the hon. member had in his mind when he began his questions.

speechtext:

subsubtopic: STEPS TO ERADICATE CORN DISEASE
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, I, too, have an infectious question for the Minister of Agriculture. It concerns head smut in hybrid corn. This is not a smutty question.
As the minister will know, this new disease was discovered last year in Norwich county, which suffered crop losses as high as 35 per cent. The disease is a potential danger for all corn crop areas. Testing has been done at the University of Guelph. Chemical treatment is apparently available, but it has only a 40 per cent effective rate.
Will the minister inform the House what specific action he undertook with regard to corn smut when he met with the corn industry and, in terms of the infected corn, will he tell us what action will be taken?

speakeroldname: Hon. E. F. Whelan (Minister of Agriculture):
subsubtopic: STEPS TO ERADICATE CORN DISEASE
speechtext: Madam Speaker, the disease mentioned by the hon. member can cause severe economic losses to corn producers. There are certain varieties of corn which are more susceptible to this disease than others. It can cause anywhere from 10 per cent to 40 per cent loss in crop production.

subsubtopic: STEPS TO ERADICATE CORN DISEASE
speechtext: Answer the question.

subsubtopic: STEPS TO ERADICATE CORN DISEASE
speechtext: My department has been running tests on the seed corn, and those companies which have the varieties with corn smut spores on them have been told to withdraw that seed corn from the market. However, in case there are some infected corn seeds on the market, the crop losses which could be suffered by those producers or the growers of commercial corn who buy that corn seed will be covered by crop insurance.

subsubtopic: STEPS TO ERADICATE CORN DISEASE
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, in view of the horrendous danger this disease presents to farm crops, will the minister, then, not order the seven identified hybrids to be taken from
May 6, 1980

the market by the four companies that are marketing them? "Yes", or "No"?

subsubtopic: STEPS TO ERADICATE CORN DISEASE
speechtext: Madam Speaker, the hon. member mentioned earlier a meeting which I held with some of the representatives of the seed corn industry, both producers and companies. We are standing by our instructions to these groups, that those known seeds which are infected with the head smut spores be withdrawn from the market.

subsubtopic: CNR AND CPR PENSION PLANS-ACTION ON RECOMMENDATIONS OF HALL REPORT
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, I had intended to put my question to the Minister of Transport, but he seems to have eluded us momentarily. In his absence, I shall put it to the Minister of Labour. It is a question which concerns both ministers. The question arises from the report of Dr. Noel Hall on Canadian Railway pension plans which was submitted a few years ago to the then minister of labour, now the Minister of Indian Affairs and Northern Development.
In view of the fact that neither the Canadian National Railways nor the Canadian Pacific Railway has taken any substantial steps to meet the recommendations of Dr. Noel Hall for improving the pensions of railway workers, will the Minister of Labour or the Minister of Transport-now that he has returned to his seat-make representations to these railway companies to consider this report, bearing in mind that both railways have received many advantages and many benefits from the taxpayers of Canada?

speakerposition: Minister of Amateur Sport; Minister of Labour
subsubtopic: CNR AND CPR PENSION PLANS-ACTION ON RECOMMENDATIONS OF HALL REPORT
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, l thank the distinguished and honourable gentleman for his question. I must say to him that, while it has not appeared that there have been dramatic results on the recommendations of the Hall commission of a number of years ago on pensions in the railways, nevertheless both the Canadian National and the Canadian Pacific have made changes in the time period involved which have improved the pensions.
Those changes perhaps are more attributable to negotiations with the unions involved than anything else, but some of them do reflect the goals that were laid out in the Hall report.

subsubtopic: CNR AND CPR PENSION PLANS-ACTION ON RECOMMENDATIONS OF HALL REPORT
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, may I say to the Minister of Labour that the view of our railway pensioners is slightly different from the view of the Minister of Labour.
However, as a supplementary question, may I ask either of the ministers-no, I think I shall ask this one of the Minister of Transport: In view of the fact that Dr. Hall made, as a major recommendation, the proposition that the Canadian Pacific Railway should at least bring its pension standards up to those of the Canadian National Railways, will the Minister
Oral Questions
of Transport carry that recommendation to the Canadian Pacific Railway, perhaps with more effectiveness than was done by the Hon. Otto Lang.

subsubtopic: CNR AND CPR PENSION PLANS-ACTION ON RECOMMENDATIONS OF HALL REPORT
speechtext: For today, Madam Speaker, I can only promise to do my best to bring about this accomplishment.

subsubtopic: CNR AND CPR PENSION PLANS-ACTION ON RECOMMENDATIONS OF HALL REPORT
speechtext: Not good enough.

subsubtopic: ILLEGAL OCCUPATION OF LAND IN KOUCHIBOUGUAC PARK, NEW BRUNSWICK
speechtext:
Madam Speaker, I would like to address a question to the Minister of the Environment who is responsible for Parks Canada. As the minister is aware, a dissident group is presently illegally occupying land in Kouchibouguac Park, New Brunswick.
The dissidents have exhausted every legal avenue in an attempt to regain this land. They have threatened to exercise force in their efforts to realize their goals, and already there has been violence. What positive measures is the minister taking to resolve this conflict once and for all, and what is he doing to ensure the safety and protection of those brave souls who might venture into Kouchibouguac Park for recreation?

subsubtopic: ILLEGAL OCCUPATION OF LAND IN KOUCHIBOUGUAC PARK, NEW BRUNSWICK
speechtext: Bring in the British commandos.

subsubtopic: ILLEGAL OCCUPATION OF LAND IN KOUCHIBOUGUAC PARK, NEW BRUNSWICK

on this particular matter-in an effort to get the matter resolved.

speechtext:
